By way of the present petition filed under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India read with section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, the petitioners seek quashing of order dated 06.11.2025 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Patiala House Court, New Delhi emanating from proceedings in FIR No.337/2016 dated 27.04.2016 registered under sections 420/406/422/424/409/120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at P.S.:
Vasant Kunj South, New Delhi.

sentences.text:
well as Mr. Sundeep Goel and Mr. Kumar Kshitij, learned counsel appearing for respondents Nos. 2 and 3.
3.

The essence of the challenge is:
3.1. Firstly, that the learned Magistrate had no power to review his own order dated 23.03.2021, by adding a condition amounting to a travel restriction vid order dated 15.02.2025; and 3.2.

Secondly, that the learned Magistrate had no power to 'clarify'
order dated 23.03.2021 read with order dated 15.02.2025, after the later order had already been set-aside by the learned Sessions Court vid judgment dated 24.07.2025, and the matter had been remanded to the learned Magistrate for reconsideration.

4. In the course of the hearing however, learned counsel appearing for respondents Nos.2 and 3 (complainants) submits, that even while order dated 06.11.2025 passed by the learned Magistrate was in force and the petitioners had already filed the present writ petition, which was pending before this court, petitioners Nos.1 and 2 have traveled abroad on 04 occasions and 11 occasions respectively, in breach and violation of the said order.
It is argued that this conduct of the petitioners disentitles them from any relief in the present proceedings.
5. Learned counsel for respondents Nos.2 and 3 has handed-up a chart dated 03.02.2026 showing the dates of travel of the petitioners.
The same is taken on record.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 09/02/2026 at 20:33:47 6.

Mr. Kshitij Garg, learned counsel for the State confirms what has been contended by learned counsel for respondents Nos.2 and 3, namely that the petitioners have travelled abroad even when there was no stay on order dated 06.11.2025 passed by the learned Magistrate.
7. Mr. Sud has also handed-up 02 separate charts dated 04.02.2026, disputing the dates of travel indicated in the chart handed-up by respondents Nos. 2 and 3.
The said two charts of petitioners are also taken on record.

8. In the circumstances, before proceeding further with the matter, the petitioners are directed to file affidavits explaining the reason why they travelled abroad in the teeth of order dated 06.11.2025 passed by the learned Magistrate, knowing full-well about the travel restraint imposed by that order,
without complying with the conditions imposed vid order dated 06.11.2025 passed by the learned Magistrate, and even when the present petition was pending.
